negative_findings.description: No dedicated Slovak POS/acquiring/terminal industry conference was found. sk queries on payments conferences returned general fintech/banking events (Finweek, FinNext, ITAPA) rather than an acceptance/terminal-specific venue.
negative_findings.result_summary: Payments-hardware and acquiring topics appear only as sessions inside broader conferences, not as standalone SK events.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Acceptance-side milestones (terminal counts, softPOS, eKasa integration) must be harvested from session-level programmes rather than from a single dedicated venue - raises collection cost and the chance of missing a signal.

negative_findings.description: LinkedIn - the seed query's named channel for CEO/bank milestone announcements - is login-walled and its ToS restricts automated collection. Search returned only company/profile landing pages, no post-level content.
negative_findings.result_summary: Individual milestone posts could not be enumerated from open search; only the company page URL and secondary reporting of post content were obtainable.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A core surface of this cell (executive communication) cannot be collected automatically without a licensed feed; the routine must plan for manual monitoring or accept lag via press-room mirrors.

negative_findings.description: No page was fetched directly in this pass; all candidate URLs come from search-result metadata and snippets. Liveness, robots.txt posture and paywall status are therefore hypotheses, not verdicts.
negative_findings.result_summary: All URLs recorded unverified by design; deterministic liveness pass required.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream collectors must not assume any URL here is reachable; a 403 on e.g. mastercard.com or forbes.sk should be read as bot-defence, not as a dead source.

negative_findings.description: Two apparently distinct Slovak fintech association web presences were found - finas.sk (FINAS, active meetups, awards, expansion hub) and slovakfintech.sk (eventy/novinky, Open Banking platform). Their relationship (rename, split, or two bodies) was not resolved.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both listed as separate candidates pending clarification.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Risk of double-counting the same association's events, or of dropping the still-active one if they are merged incorrectly.

negative_findings.description: No established Slovak-language term was identified for 'earnings call' / 'investor day' in the SK bank context - SK banks are largely subsidiaries of foreign groups (Erste, Intesa, RBI, KBC) and do not hold local earnings calls, so the spoken-disclosure channel is conferences and awards rather than IR events.
negative_findings.result_summary: sk queries for executive result presentations returned conference and award content, not IR calls.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the premise of this cell: for SK, group-level IR (Vienna/Milan/Brussels) plus local conference/award stages together substitute for a domestic earnings-call channel; the routine should also watch parent-group IR.

coverage_gaps.description: Video/audio archives beyond the TechEvents YouTube channel were not enumerated - individual bank YouTube channels, ITAPA session recordings and podcast formats (where CEOs speak at length) remain unmapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated sk pass on 'podcast bankovnictvo Slovensko', 'zaznam konferencie', and per-bank YouTube channels; capture channel IDs for API-based transcript collection.

coverage_gaps.description: Non-bank SK payment actors (PSPs, acquirers, softPOS vendors, e-money institutions) were only reached indirectly via association pages; no member directory was retrieved.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch the FINAS member list and NBS register of payment/e-money institutions, then check each actor for conference-speaking and award participation.

coverage_gaps.description: Historical depth is thin: only ~2023-2026 editions of the awards and conferences were surfaced, though Zlata minca runs since 2005 and TREND's awards for 27+ years.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Backfill via site archives and the Wayback Machine to build a 10-year longitudinal award/winner series usable as a competitive-position proxy.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language SK event surfaces (international editions, CEE conferences where SK banks speak, e.g. Finweek Kuala Lumpur, FinTech Roadmap) were only lightly covered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add an en-language pass targeting CEE/EU payment conferences with SK speaker participation to catch expansion and roadmap statements made abroad.

coverage_gaps.description: No award-submission documents themselves were located - only nomination lists and result press releases. Submission dossiers (where the richest unpublished numbers would sit) may not be public at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Contact organisers (Zlata minca, Mastercard/Visa SK, TREND) to establish whether submission summaries or jury materials are ever published; otherwise record as structurally unavailable.

brief: Slovakia's spoken/event disclosure channel is small, dense and highly repeatable: a handful of annual fixtures - Finweek Bratislava (with the TechEvents YouTube archive as its verbatim record), NBS's own conference series and IBV NBS's FinNext, ITAPA for state-driven payments infrastructure, and Forbes Money events - carry almost all executive strategy talk, while four award programmes (Zlata minca, TREND 'Banka roka', Mastercard Awards SK, Visa Awards SK) periodically publish competitive rankings that banks do not disclose themselves. The scheme awards are the standout find: Mastercard's SK release explicitly names the leading card issuer by absolute transaction count and the leading acceptor, making it a rare volume proxy released months out of cycle. The main structural constraint is that SK banks are foreign-group subsidiaries with no domestic earnings calls, so this event layer plus parent-group IR jointly substitutes for spoken financial disclosure; the main collection constraint is LinkedIn, the natural CEO-milestone surface, which is login-walled and ToS-restricted and will need manual or licensed monitoring. All URLs here are unverified by design and await the deterministic liveness pass.
